m0_comparator.policy: The authoritative frozen M0 OOF artifact is consumed directly. M0 raw probabilities are not numerically regenerated under a later dependency solve.

feature_contract.orientation_policy: All model inputs are antisymmetric under fighter swap; fit_intercept=false.

regularization.selection: Nested expanding chronological inner OOF pooled log loss; exact ties choose smaller C.

validation_note.reason: The first harness numerically regenerated M0 raw probabilities and correctly failed the frozen M0 OOF hash guard under a later dependency solve.
validation_note.resolution: The comparator was changed to load and verify the authoritative frozen M0 Actions artifact directly. A successful precursor run at 45f080d produced the same substantive M1 result; after that only M0 row-key normalization/provenance changed. The authoritative accepted run is 34718520686.

limitations: M1 is a validation benchmark, not a production betting model.
No sportsbook odds, market probabilities, ROI, Kelly, price thresholds, or market-specific tuning are used.
No tree, boosting, neural, ensemble, AutoML, opponent-adjustment, or simulator methodology is introduced.

The broad F02 surface materially improves M0, but the strong preference for C=0.01 in 11 of 12 outer folds shows that substantial regularization is necessary and the lower edge of the predeclared grid is frequently preferred.
M1 expected calibration error is 0.01809 versus 0.01465 for M0, so calibration-bin error did not improve even though log loss and Brier did.
Light Heavyweight remains a materially weak slice: N=412, log loss 0.69489, Brier 0.25032, accuracy 54.61%, AUC 0.5788.
The largest mean absolute coefficient is the reach_cm missingness difference, indicating meaningful dependence on data-availability patterns that warrants later robustness review.

Exact raw-float M1 OOF hashes differed across two successful hosted runs despite essentially identical metrics and unchanged M1 methodology; the accepted runtime artifact is the authoritative identity and bitwise rerun determinism is not claimed.
2026 is the partial latest-year fold represented by frozen F02.

self_review.question: Did M1 improve the frozen M0 winner benchmark using only the governed F02 surface under chronological validation and predeclared regularization selection?

light_heavyweight.interpretation: M1 improves the frozen M0 Light Heavyweight slice but the slice remains materially weak and close to an uninformative probability benchmark.

coefficient_diagnostics.interpretation: The strongest average coefficient is a reach-data missingness difference. This is not target leakage under the chronological fold-local design, but it shows M1 relies materially on data-availability patterns and should receive a dedicated robustness/data-quality audit before production use.

initial_full_run.reason: Frozen M0 comparator OOF hash mismatch when the harness regenerated M0 probabilities under a later numerical dependency solve.

performance_governance.changes_after_first_successful_performan: Only frozen-M0 row-key normalization and comparator/provenance documentation changed. M1 feature construction, model family, C grid, nested selection rule, and validation population did not change.
performance_governance.floating_point_reproducibility_note: The two successful hosted runs agree in verdict and aggregate metrics to roughly 1e-11 but have different exact OOF logical hashes. The accepted Actions artifact is therefore the authoritative raw-float identity; bitwise OOF rerun determinism is not claimed.
